body:
Part of #289; coordinate #290/#235. Author dispatch depends on reviewed, frozen candidates from the judgment-boundary and constructor-admission experiments. This is a distinct trial from #108 and must not select or prepare #108's theorem.

## Question

Do the candidate interfaces remove repeated semantic-annotation work while preserving the same independently specified dependent argument and observations?

## Acceptance

- Freeze mathematical acceptance conditions, supported fragments, interface snapshots, task order, reference artifacts, assistance, exposure, budgets and stopping rules before fresh independent authors begin. Separate public calibration from at least one held-out task selected after the interface freeze.
- Compare a retained baseline with the candidate on equivalent mathematical requirements. Use authors unexposed to private solutions or the other arm, and preserve commands, immutable source attempts, failures and diagnostics. Record unavailable configuration or usage data instead of inferring it.
- Include repeated dependent substitution and reuse after the selected constructor extension. Exercise the admitted identity/witness behavior. If a higher-capability claim is evaluated, require the separate concrete higher-model evidence before freezing that claim; a restricted trial must state its scope and cannot discharge the higher adoption gate.
- Assess source judgments, selected data, compatibility laws and caller obligations, not only successful target calculations. Classify remaining work as mathematical requirement, model-builder coherence, interface/presentation burden, host encoding or missing documentation. A caller record requesting all old annotation alignments does not count as removing them.
- Account separately for preparation, reference proofs, support engineering, author work and coordinator repairs. Do not interpret a small agent sample as causal productivity evidence or human-usability validation. Preserve exact accepted submissions and replay them through required validation.
- Make a repair/adopt/revise/defer decision grounded in the observations; keep failed candidates as evidence. New source snapshots after repairs require a new frozen round. Preserve #107/#108's separate ownership, public-history integrity and independent theorem gate.

## Evidence and boundaries

Use `docs/research/dependent-architecture-reassessment.md`, its three independent assessments, #292's report and frozen external memo as starting evidence. Consult primary sources for the claims actually used. These are competing diagnoses and proposals, not new checked theorems. The work is scoped by its mathematical questions, not an arbitrary effort cap. Substantial reconstruction or a different foundation is an allowed outcome; an immediate adapter to current generated annotations is not a condition for investigating it.

Keep object-language identity, judgmental equality, metatheoretic equality and presentation comparisons distinct. State which observations an interpretation preserves; a deliberately lossy interpretation is not invalid merely because it is not faithful. Require exact selected data when the client contract calls for it. Separate model-builder work, ordinary author work and host-language encoding cost.

Persist findings, failed approaches, positive constructions, exact hypotheses and the adopt/investigate/defer/reject decision. New Lean claims require checked specializations, statement review and README's applicable build/exhaustive audit. Research and implementation require independent Standards/Spec review. This issue does not resume #107, select or prepare #108's fresh theorem, activate #260, require a new frontend, or authorize weakening the mathematical acceptance conditions.

## Coordination

Blocked by #315 and #317 for author dispatch. The freeze must also have #316 evidence for any claimed dependent higher capability. Restricted trials may proceed without that claim and cannot satisfy its adoption gate. #108 remains a separately gated experiment.
title: Compare frozen dependent author interfaces after interpretation and extension experiments
